from typing import Tuple, Any

def check_type(tup: Tuple[Any, ...]) -> bool:
    """
    Checks if all elements in the given tuple have the same data type.
    
    Args:
        tup (Tuple): The input tuple to be checked.
        
    Returns:
        bool: True if all types are identical, False otherwise.
              Raises an error if the tuple is empty or contains mixed None/other edge cases depending on preference.
    """
    # Handle empty tuple case explicitly (usually considered "all same" vacuously true)
    if not tup:
        return True
    
    first_type = type(tup[0])
    
    for item in tup:
        if type(item) != first_type:
            return False
            
    return True

# Test cases provided in the prompt and additional examples
if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Original requirement
    assert check_type((5, 6, 7, 3, 5, 6)) == True
    
    # Additional test: Mixed types (should be False)
    assert check_type((1, "a", [2])) == False
    
    # Additional test: All strings (should be True)
    assert check_type(("x", "y", "z")) == True
    
    print("All assertions passed!")
